# Enforced rules

This catalog lists every rule that a gate enforces. A script generates it from the rule sources, so it cannot drift from them.

- A reviewer does not report a violation of a rule here. The gate already fails on it.
- The rules that no gate enforces are in [review-checklist.md](./review-checklist.md).
- To choose a gate for a new rule, read [gate-design.md](./gate-design.md).

When you add, remove or change a rule in `.oxlintrc.json`, a JS plugin, `scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs`, `scripts/test-tautology-rules.mjs`, `package.json` or `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, run `pnpm rules:catalog`. `pnpm check:rules-catalog` fails while this file is stale.

## Lint rules: oxlint built-ins

`pnpm lint` fails on each rule below. A type-aware rule reads the type of an expression (rung 2 in gate-design.md). ## Lint rules: `alfred` plugin

`pnpm lint` fails on each rule below. The description is the rule's own `meta.docs.description`.

| Rule | Scope | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alfred/hand-rolled-key-guard` |  | Test a key of a closed table with `keyGuard(TABLE)` from `@alfred/contracts`, not by hand. |
| `alfred/log-caught-error-under-err` |  | Reject a caught error, or its message, in a `logger` call anywhere but as the raw value under `err`. |
| `alfred/motion-safe-variant-animate` |  | Require `motion-safe:` on a variant-prefixed `animate-*` utility on an element that has `motion-reduce:animate-none`. |
| `alfred/no-conditional-motion-ref` |  | Reject a conditional `ref` on a `motion` element, which reads its ref only at mount. |
| `alfred/no-constants-re-export` |  | Disallow re-exporting a constants module's value from a module that is not its barrel. |
| `alfred/no-dash-in-web-copy` |  | Reject an em dash or an en dash in a web string or JSX text. |
| `alfred/no-delta-class-utility-collision` |  | Reject a `scale-*` utility on an `app-press` element without `not-active:`, and a `translate-*` utility on an `app-hover-lift` element. |
| `alfred/no-exported-hasher` |  | Disallow exporting a function whose parameter flows into a hash digest from a module that is not a hash owner. |
| `alfred/no-function-wrapper-shim` |  | Disallow an exported function whose only job is to return a constant or an imported name. |
| `alfred/no-never-sentinel-binding` |  | Reject a `never` binding in a `switch` clause; close the switch with `assertNever`. |
| `alfred/no-type-alias-shim` |  | Disallow exporting a bare new name for an imported type. |
| `alfred/no-type-re-export-shim` |  | Disallow re-exporting a constants module's type from a module that is not its barrel. |
| `alfred/no-union-enum-without-default` |  | Require an explicit `default` on every Elysia `t.UnionEnum` call. |
| `alfred/sha256-over-json-stringify` |  | Disallow a hash digest over JSON.stringify output, whose pre-image depends on object key order. |
| `alfred/switch-literal-needs-default` |  | Require a `default` clause on a `switch` whose `case` tests are all string literals. |
| `alfred/transition-names-individual-transform` |  | Require a `transition-[…transform…]` list to name the `scale`, `translate` or `rotate` property that the element writes. |

## Import fences: `no-restricted-imports`

`pnpm lint` fails when a file imports a specifier in a group below. An override that does not restate a group allows that group in its files. `pnpm check:oxlint-config` keeps each restated group identical to the root group.

| Specifiers | Allowed in | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@alfred/assistant/knowledge/internal` | `apps/server/src/scripts/**` | The knowledge internal tooling door is restricted to apps/server/src/scripts/** (see packages/assistant/src/knowledge/internal.ts). Import the sanctioned contract from @alfred/assistant/knowledge instead. |
| `@alfred/integrations/google/internal` | `packages/assistant/src/connections/ingestion/gmail-ingest.ts` | The raw Gmail watch primitive is restricted to its one allowlisted friend file (see packages/integrations/src/google/internal.ts). Install a watch through installGmailWatchAndSeedCursor from @alfred/assistant/connections/ingestion, which also seeds the ingestion_state cursor; a raw installGmailWatch leaves the credential cursorless. |
| `@alfred/assistant/connections/ingestion/internal` | `apps/server/src/scripts/**`; `packages/assistant/test/gmail-ingest.test.ts` | The raw Gmail ingestion entry points are restricted to the operational scripts under apps/server/src/scripts/** and the ingestion-cursor test packages/assistant/test/gmail-ingest.test.ts (see packages/assistant/src/connections/ingestion/internal.ts). Import the sanctioned contract from @alfred/assistant/connections/ingestion instead, which drives ingestion through the BullMQ job that owns retry, burst dedup and the ingestion_state cursor. |
| `@alfred/assistant/tool-runtime/internal/registry` | nowhere | The global tool catalog is restricted to packages/assistant/src/tool-runtime/ (see packages/assistant/src/tool-runtime/internal/registry.ts, which owns the one mutable map). Import the sanctioned contract from @alfred/assistant/tool-runtime instead, whose index re-exports the catalog surface. |
| `@alfred/assistant/tool-runtime/internal/*`, `@alfred/assistant/tool-runtime/internal/**` | nowhere | Every module under packages/assistant/src/tool-runtime/internal/ is private to packages/assistant/src/tool-runtime/, not one door but the whole directory. Import the sanctioned contract from @alfred/assistant/tool-runtime instead, whose index publishes the runtime surface. The narrower @alfred/assistant/tool-runtime/internal/registry group above is deliberately kept beside this one: a specifier holding a glob is gated on package existence alone, so the literal registry specifier is the only one in this family that `pnpm check:oxlint-config` still resolves through the exports map to a git-listed file. |
| `effect`, `effect/*` | `packages/assistant/src/connections/mcp/manager.ts` | The effect library is restricted to packages/assistant/src/connections/mcp/manager.ts, the one Effect module in Alfred (ADR-0114). Write async/await here. A second Effect module needs its own ADR or an amendment to ADR-0114 with its own evidence, and then a new allowlist override in this file. |
| `@alfred/http`, `@alfred/http/*`, `@alfred/http/**`, `.`, `./index*`, `..`, `../index*`, `../..`, `../../index*` | Applies only in `packages/http/src/**` | packages/http/src may not import its own root barrel. `@alfred/http` and every relative spelling of src/index.ts resolve to the barrel that re-exports this file, so the import closes an `index.ts -> this file -> index.ts` module cycle. That cycle compiles, passes every gate and boots; it becomes a TDZ ReferenceError the day someone reorders the exports in index.ts. Import the concrete sibling module instead, e.g. `./middleware/auth`. |

## Consolidation rows: `pnpm check:consolidation`

A `gate` row fails `pnpm check`. `.claude/hooks/helper-hints.mjs` also shows each row's fix at edit time. A line that ends in `// drift-ok: <reason>` is exempt.

| Row | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `as-loose-record` | Use isRecord/toRecord from @alfred/contracts for a genuine open object, or parse the known projection with its owning schema. An assertion does not validate the boundary. |
| `as-string-array` | Use toStringArray(x) from @alfred/contracts — it checks the element type at runtime instead of asserting it. |
| `as-tool-name` | Narrow the string with isToolName from @alfred/contracts before indexing a ToolName record or dispatching. Don't assert it. |
| `boot-error-plain-extends` | A handler-registry boot error must `extends TriggerConsumerBootError` (import it from the triggers barrel, `from "@alfred/assistant/triggers"`), not plain Error — the publish seam only exempts a TriggerConsumerBootError from the best-effort swallow, so a plain-Error boot failure is silently no-op'd instead of failing the job. If this No…RegisteredError is a runtime not-found rather than a registry-wiring boot error, append `// drift-ok: <reason>`. |
| `bullmq-job-timestamp` | Use scheduledFireTime(job) from @alfred/assistant/execution for the time a job scheduler fired this job for. BullMQ sets job.timestamp when it creates the job, one interval before a scheduled job runs. For when the job really started, read job.processedOn. If the value is an identity, not a time, append `// drift-ok: <what it identifies>`. |
| `canonical-param-key` | Use canonicalParamKey(key) from @alfred/contracts — the one canonical key-folding function. |
| `chat-tool-preview-reparse` | Read `args` / `result` off ResolvedToolCall from ~/lib/chat/resolved-tool-call. resolveToolCall parses both previews one time, at the stream fold and the persisted split. Take a ResolvedToolCall (or a Pick of it) as the parameter instead of a raw preview string. |
| `db-backed-skip-hand-rolled` | Use dbBackedSkip("database") from ./support/db-backed in this test tree — it skips on a laptop with no Postgres and THROWS when CI is set, so a job that reached no service cannot exit 0. Do not hand-roll a `{ skip }` on a service variable. If this line is not a skip guard, append `// drift-ok: <reason>`. |
| `email-domain-split` | Use parseMailbox(value)?.domain from @alfred/contracts. A split on the first `@` reads the wrong domain when the local part holds one. |
| `error-to-message` | Use toMessage(err) from @alfred/contracts — the one caught-error-to-string helper. |
| `export-star-outside-root-barrel` | Name each re-export: `export { a, type B } from "./x"`, with only the names that importers read through this barrel. Only the two package root barrels (packages/contracts/src/index.ts, packages/db/src/schemas.ts) may use `export *`. |
| `hand-built-api-error` | Throw an Errors.* factory from @alfred/contracts — `throw Errors.NotFoundError("…")`. It owns the code-to-status pairing. Catch with isApiError(err, "NOT_FOUND") rather than a per-kind class. |
| `hand-rolled-domain-match` | Use isDomainOrSubdomain(domain, base) from @alfred/contracts. It matches whole labels and expects normalized (lowercase) values, as emailDomain and normalizeDomain return them. For a proper subdomain only, keep the bare endsWith. |
| `hand-rolled-nested-transaction` | Use runAtomic(runner, body) from @alfred/db/helpers — `.transaction()` on a handle you already hold is a hand-rolled savepoint. `db().transaction(` is the sanctioned root-client spelling and does not match; a Better-Auth/DI adapter's own `transaction` method is a different interface and carries a `// drift-ok:` comment block above the call. |
| `hand-rolled-no-reply-regex` | Call classifyLocalPart(localPart) from @alfred/contracts. It returns the sender class (automated, role, group, none) and how the word matched (whole, edge, token). Map that result to your output through a total `satisfies Record<MatchedSenderClass, Record<LocalPartMatch, …>>` table. Add a new word to SENDER_WORDS in sender-class.ts, not to a local list. |
| `hand-rolled-object-closure` | Call closesOpenAsk(provider, kind, category, proof) from @alfred/contracts for a projection row — `proof` is the reading you actually hold, and a sync reader with no IO holds `stored_projection` — or evidenceObjectClosesAsk(card.object) for an evidence card, or closureCandidate(provider, kind, category) when you only mean to nominate a candidate for a consumer that will go get the proof. All read the registry's per-kind closesAskOn and closesAskFrom, so a kind that closes on neither category stays correct, and both return the closing category rather than a boolean. `failed` closes nothing: it is terminal for the object but it opens a CI loop, which is why a terminal-means-closed helper is not the reader either — if you truly mean terminal for the object and not closed, say so in a `// drift-ok:` marker. |
| `hand-rolled-timezone-validator` | Use isIanaTimezone from @alfred/contracts — the one memoized, alias-aware timezone validator. Don't hand-roll an Intl.DateTimeFormat trial. |
| `hand-rolled-utc-offset-parse` | Use inZone(timezone).offsetMs(instant) from @alfred/assistant/time — the one place the longOffset string is parsed. inZone(tz).clock(instant).utcOffset gives the signed ISO fragment. |
| `hand-rolled-whitespace-collapse` | Call collapseWhitespace(text) from @alfred/contracts — one fold for every display snippet, preview, title and summary. Keep a private fold, plus `// drift-ok: <what the value identifies>`, only when other code compares the value byte for byte: a key, a hash, a dedup token, a cache lookup, or a query a provider must receive unchanged. The row also fires on a fold that must NOT trim — `out += chunk.replace(/\s+/g, " ")` builds one string from many pieces, and `collapseWhitespace` would eat the edge space that separates them — so mark that case the same way. Being stored is not that test and neither is being read by a classifier — prose a person or a model reads is a display fold either way. |
| `hand-split-oauth-scope` | Use parseOAuthScopeList(scope) from @alfred/contracts — the one grammar that accepts both RFC 6749 space lists and GitHub's comma list. |
| `humanize-integration-slug` | Index INTEGRATION_DISPLAY_NAMES[slug] from @alfred/contracts with a typed IntegrationSlug, or call integrationDisplayName(value) for an unchecked string. A LoopEntityProvider (MCP identity provider) reads loopEntityProviderName(provider). humanizeSlug is for action and field slugs, not integration names. |
| `module-scope-settings-bind` | Bind settings({ userId }) inside the request, workflow step, or job item that reads it. A bind keeps its first load and never re-reads, so a module-scope bind serves a stale zone and stale flags until the process restarts. |
| `oauth-state-primitive` | Bind oauthHandshake(PROVIDER) — or oauthHandshake("mcp") for an MCP authorization — from @alfred/assistant/connections once per route module; call .begin({ userId }) on connect and .complete(state) on callback. It signs, remembers and consumes the nonce, and checks the user, in one operation. |
| `object-state-row-lock-mode` | Lock an `integration_objects` row with `.for("no key update")`, through lockIdentityRow in ./store.ts. A key upsert takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on its parent object row, which waits behind `FOR UPDATE` and re-opens the cross-table deadlock the two-phase lock order closes. If this lock is over another table, append `// drift-ok: <table, and why its mode is free>`. |
| `partial-integration-slug-record` | Derive the table from INTEGRATIONS in @alfred/contracts (a projection over the record), or key it `satisfies Record<…Slug, T>` on a derived union (LiveProviderSlug, CatalogSlug, SupportedPassthroughSlug) so a missing integration is a compile error. If an absent slug genuinely means something (a sparse per-user override), append `// drift-ok: <what absence means>`. |
| `raw-agent-run-status-sql` | Do not write agent_runs.status with raw SQL. Route lifecycle transitions through the owning agent service/executor door. |
| `raw-gmail-token-call` | Call gmailMailbox({ credentialId }) from @alfred/integrations/google and use its methods (listMessages, getMessage, batchModifyMessages, …). Each call resolves a fresh token through getFreshAccessToken, so no caller holds one. Inside the package, gmailMailboxFor(resolver) binds another resolver. |
| `raw-ioredis-construction` | Use createRedisConnection(kind) from @alfred/db/redis. Its RedisConnectionKind table is the one place that decides what a connection does during an outage — a hand-built client silently picks "waits forever". |
| `raw-palette-color` | Use an `app-*` token from apps/web/src/index.css. Status: `text-app-{red,amber,green}-4` for text and solid fills, `-1` for a tint fill, `-2` for its border or ring, and `text-app-bg-1` for ink on a solid `-4` fill. On a fixed dark surface (video, lightbox, overlay), add `app-media` to its root and use `text-app-fg-a{1..4}` / `bg-app-bg-a{1..4}` for white-alpha ink and fills. |
| `raw-process-env` | Use serverEnv() from @alfred/env/server — the only sanctioned reader of process env. It validates the whole environment once against a schema. |
| `raw-radius-class` | Use a role tier from apps/web/src/index.css: `rounded-control-xs` (20px and smaller: kbd, checkbox, tag), `rounded-control-sm` (24-28px controls), `rounded-control` (32-40px buttons, rows, inputs, menu items), `rounded-surface` (cards, banners, menus, popovers), `rounded-panel` (shell, sidebar, rail, composer, dialogs), or `rounded-full` for pills. Pick by what the element is, and give a container its inner tier plus its padding. |
| `raw-user-preferences-query` | Read and write user_preferences through settings({ userId[, exec: tx] }) from @alfred/assistant/settings: get / all / timezone / flags for reads (one SELECT per bind), set / setIfUnset / delete for writes. Pass the bind the flow already holds instead of taking a second one. |
| `read-write-github-mcp-endpoint` | Use GITHUB_MCP_ENDPOINT_HREF from @alfred/assistant — Alfred pins GitHub's read-only resource `/mcp/readonly` (ADR-0094). The `/mcp` root also serves write tools. |
| `replicache-subscribe-outside-helper` | Use useReplicacheSubscription(query, select?, { isEmpty? }) from ~/lib/replicache/use-replicache-subscription. It owns the one loading rule and keeps cached rows through a sync error. |
| `spread-over-defaults` | Use withDefaults(DEFAULTS, overrides) from @alfred/contracts — it ignores override keys whose value is undefined, so a default can't be zeroed by a present-undefined. |
| `sql-any-of-interpolated-list` | Use inArray(expr, list) from drizzle-orm inside the template (`WHERE ${inArray(sql`lower(alias)`, list)}`), or pass one array parameter with a cast: `ANY(${sql.param(list)}::text[])`. |
| `suppression-without-reason` | Name every rule the directive suppresses, in the spelling the config uses, then give the reason after ` -- `: `// oxlint-disable-next-line <plugin>/<rule> -- <why this line is the exception>`. See docs/reference/gate-design.md § Suppressions and disarms. |
| `unfiltered-event-receipt-read` | Read typedEventReceipts from @alfred/db/schemas. Only the view definition, receipt conflict read-back, the deliver job (publishes both tiers), raw inventory, corpus backfill, and payload retention may read both tiers of eventReceipts. |
| `unguarded-agent-run-status-upsert` | Do not upsert agent_runs.status. Route lifecycle transitions through the owning agent service/executor door so terminal-state and attempt guards cannot be bypassed. |
| `unguarded-agent-run-status-write` | Route `agent_runs.status` writes through commitGuardedRunUpdate in packages/api/src/modules/agent/executor.ts — it takes the row lock, refuses a superseded attempt, and refuses to write a live status over a terminal one. A bare .where(eq(agentRuns.id, …)) resurrects cancelled runs (#530). If the transaction already holds FOR UPDATE on the row and has checked the status under that lock (leaseRun's backstop), append `// drift-ok: <that reason>` to the `.update(agentRuns)` line. |
| `unowned-live-confirmation-proof` | Pass the proof you actually hold to closesOpenAsk(provider, kind, category, proof) from @alfred/contracts. A reader over a stored integration_objects row holds `stored_projection`; only a caller that just took a live provider read of THIS object may name `live_confirmation`. If you mean to nominate a candidate for a consumer that will go get the read, call closureCandidate(provider, kind, category) and hand on its `proof` instead of naming one. A new site that genuinely takes the read joins this rule's `owners`; a one-off states the read it holds in a `// drift-ok:` marker. |

These `hint` rows do not fail a build. They advise at edit time only.

| Row | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `hand-rolled-domain-literal-match` | Use isDomainOrSubdomain(domain, "sentry.io") from @alfred/contracts. It expects normalized (lowercase) values, as emailDomain and normalizeDomain return them. |
| `hand-rolled-enum-guard` | Build the guard once with enumGuard(TUPLE) from @alfred/contracts — it narrows `unknown` to `typeof TUPLE[number]` with no cast and no SAFETY comment. The tuple stays the single source of truth; a per-site `(TUPLE as readonly string[]).includes(value)` is a fourth spelling of it. |
| `hand-rolled-record-guard` | isRecord(x) from @alfred/contracts is this check. Use toRecord(x) if you want a Record or {} back rather than a boolean. |
| `object-keys-cast` | Over a closed const table, use typedKeys(TABLE) / typedEntries(TABLE) from @alfred/contracts. To build a record over a key tuple, use recordFromKeys(KEYS, (key) => value); to project one field of each entry, use pluckField(TABLE, "field"). To close a record that a loop filled, declare it Partial<Record<K, V>> and check it with hasEveryKey(record, KEYS). For keys of a value that came from outside, narrow each key with a guard instead. |
| `raw-email-normalize` | Use parseMailbox(value) from @alfred/contracts for the name, address, local part and domain of a `Name <addr>` header, or parseEmailAddress(value) for the address alone (the single source of self-mail matching). mailboxLabel(value) is the display label; splitAddressList(value) splits a To/Cc list. |
| `raw-intl-timezone` | @alfred/assistant/time owns every date/zone reading, split by one question: does the reading need a zone? NEEDS ONE — inZone(tz) binds it once and every reading is a method: .day() mints the LocalDateKey, .hour(), .offsetMs(), .clock(), .startOf(key, hour?), .dayBounds(), .format(instant). DOESN'T — a free function on the key: addDays (day math on the key, never in ms), weekdayIndex (day-of-week DECISIONS — never string-match a rendered weekday name), formatDay(key, "short"\|"long"\|"weekday"). Zones are IanaTimezone (settings({ userId }).timezone(), parseIanaTimezone); day keys are LocalDateKey (parseLocalDateKey / isLocalDateKey at a persistence or wire boundary) — both branded, so a plain string won't type-check. A bare Intl trial once broke briefings on "UTC", and a per-call-site UTC reading dated triage todos a day early. |
| `raw-json-parse` | parseJsonWith(raw, schema, fallback?) from @alfred/contracts parses AND validates in one step; safeJsonParse(raw) handles malformed input without a try/catch. Reach for those before JSON.parse + a cast. |
| `raw-provider-client` | Use route(name) from @alfred/ai instead of constructing a provider client — it carries the retry wrapper, metering, and per-model capability map. |
| `sender-regex-test` | Read the sender's domain with parseMailbox(from)?.domain from @alfred/contracts, then compare it with isDomainOrSubdomain(domain, base). A regex over the raw header also matches the display name and a look-alike host. |
| `stale-google-access-token` | Resolve Google tokens with getFreshAccessToken from @alfred/integrations/google. The persisted accessToken and a manual refresh are both the stale path — and the token is a secret, so never log or persist it on an error. |

## Test-tautology rows: `pnpm check:test-tautology`

A `gate` row fails `pnpm check`. A `// tautology-ok: <reason>` marker on the match or the comment above it exempts the match.

| Row | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `rebuilt-position-index` | Do not rebuild expected `0..N-1` from actual.length. Assert a literal `deepEqual(..., [0,1])` or loop `assert.equal(c.position, i)`. A rebuilt oracle cannot fail when `position` is wrong. |

These `hint` rows do not fail a build. They advise at edit time only.

| Row | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `literal-cap-pin-without-why` | A bare literal pin `EMBED_COST_CAP_USD == 0.5` is a change detector with no policy. Add `// why: <incident/ADR>` or delete — the math tests (`maxTokensForPrice`) already exercise the cap. If the literal must stay (policy gate), add `// tautology-ok: policy — $0.50 cap is the product limit`. |
| `self-mirroring-oracle` | Both sides call the same function — the test mirrors the SUT. Pin one side to a literal or external artifact. If intentionally cross-checking two paths (e.g. `stream()` vs `sanitizeVoice()`), anchor the shared oracle with one literal test and add `// tautology-ok: cross-check + anchored at <file:line>`. |

## Check scripts

Each script below runs in `pnpm check`, in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), or in both. The summary is the first comment paragraph of the script file.

| Script | `pnpm check` | CI | Command | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check-types` | no | yes | `turbo run check-types && tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json` |  |
| `check:architecture` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-module-architecture.mjs` |  |
| `check:campaign-state` | yes | yes | `node scripts/campaign-state.selftest.mjs` | Drives `campaign-state.mjs` against the failure it exists to prevent: two phases writing two different items of one `state.json` at the same time. |
| `check:consolidation` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-consolidation-drift.mjs` | Guards the "define once, derive everything else" consolidations against re-drift. Each `gate` rule was hand-rolled in N places, collapsed to a single canonical helper, and would silently return the moment someone types the raw idiom again. jscpd (`pnpm dup`) only *reports* duplication after the fact and nobody runs it on every change — this runs inside `pnpm check`, so a reintroduced idiom fails the same gate as a type error. |
| `check:constraint-snapshot` | yes | yes | `pnpm --filter @alfred/db check:constraint-snapshot` |  |
| `check:doc-symbols` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-doc-symbols.mjs` | Fails when a doc names a code symbol that no longer exists. |
| `check:duplicates` | yes | yes | `jscpd apps packages --threshold 1 --reporters console` |  |
| `check:exports` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-package-exports.mjs` | Fails the build when a workspace advertises an `exports` subpath whose target resolves to no file git lists. |
| `check:imports` | yes | yes | `node scripts/relative-to-alias.mjs --check` | Rewrites brittle cross-tree relative import specifiers to the `~/` alias. |
| `check:knip` | yes | yes | `knip --treat-config-hints-as-errors` |  |
| `check:merge-guard` | yes | yes | `node scripts/merge-guard.selftest.mjs` | Drives `.claude/hooks/merge-guard.mjs` against the merge it exists to stop: a merge that skips red required checks (`gh pr merge --admin`, or the REST or GraphQL merge). |
| `check:oxlint-config` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-oxlint-config.mjs` | Fails the build when oxlint would read a config other than the root one, when a root oxlint script has lost the `--config` pin that makes the root config the only one it reads, when a fence inside that config names a specifier that no longer resolves to anything, when a scoped copy of a fence has drifted from the root list it restates, and when a gitignore line hides a tracked source file from oxlint's and oxfmt's file walk — a mechanism the `--config` pin is measured NOT to close, because the walk happens before any config is consulted — and when the root `tsconfig.json` `references`, which give test and eval files their real program in the type-aware lint, drift from the tracked `tsconfig.test.json` / `tsconfig.eval.json` projects. |
| `check:oxlint-plugin` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-oxlint-plugin.mjs` | Fails when a rule in one of the repo's oxlint JS plugins is untested, unregistered, or registered but not actually enforced by the root config. |
| `check:plan-status` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-plan-status.mjs` | Fails when a plan under `docs/plans/` has no valid `status:` in its front matter. |
| `check:pr-body` | no | yes | `node scripts/check-pr-body.mjs` | Fails when the pull request for this branch does not carry the four sections `CLAUDE.md` asks for, when one closing keyword lists several issues (`Closes #1, #2`), which closes only the first on merge, when a prose sentence has more than 25 words (the ASD-STE100 limit), or when the body uses a review-process word such as `Round 1`, `r2`, `item 36` or `as on main`. |
| `check:prose-locators` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-prose-locators.mjs` | Fails when backticked prose names a repo-relative path or an `@alfred/*` specifier that resolves to nothing. |
| `check:rules-catalog` | yes | yes | `node scripts/enforced-rules-catalog.mjs --check` | Builds docs/reference/enforced-rules.md: the catalog of every rule that a gate enforces, generated from the files that define the rules. |
| `check:schema-catalog` | yes | yes | `node scripts/schema-catalog.mjs --selftest` | A discovery aid for runtime validators: where do this repo's zod schemas live, and which declared shapes look identical under different names? |
| `check:script-paths` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-script-paths.mjs` | Fails when a repository path hardcoded inside `scripts/` stops resolving. |
| `check:smells` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-smells.mjs` | Fails when a smell file breaks the catalog grammar, when a smell found in two PRs has no decision, or when a view that scripts/smells.mjs writes is stale. |
| `check:test-id-prefixes` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-test-id-prefixes.mjs` | Fails when one test file's `LIKE '<prefix>%'` cleanup can delete another test file's rows. |
| `check:test-tautology` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-test-tautology.mjs` | Guards against tautological tests — asserts that restate implementation instead of pinning a product/state/contract property. |
| `check:test-typecheck-baseline` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-test-typecheck-baseline.mjs` | Fails the build when a package's second-pass `exclude` stops describing which of its test files are actually dirty. |
| `check:type-fixtures` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-type-fixture-programs.mjs` | Fails the build when a tracked source file is read by no tsc program: a `*.type-test.ts` outside a program its own package's `check-types` runs, or a `scripts/**/*.mjs` outside `scripts/tsconfig.json`. |
| `check:web-boundaries` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-web-boundaries.mjs` | Fails the build when browser runtime code takes a value binding on a Node-only workspace package, and when the prose that restates the forbidden list has drifted from the list itself. |
| `check:web-bundle-graph` | no | yes | `node scripts/check-web-bundle-graph.mjs` | Fails the build when a Node-only package or a Node builtin is in the browser bundle, or when a workspace module the bundle contains is one the source fence does not scan. |
| `format:check` | yes | yes | `oxfmt --check --ignore-path .gitignore --ignore-path .prettierignore apps packages scripts package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml turbo.json .oxlintrc.json .oxfmtrc.json` |  |
| `lint` | yes | yes | `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --report-unused-disable-directives-severity=error` |  |
